# patientdesk-sdk

> Unofficial TypeScript SDK for PatientDesk Turkish voice models. Alania text-to-speech, Duyu speech-to-text over REST and WebSocket, and a keyless status helper. Zero runtime dependencies.

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/getting-started.md

# Getting started

`patientdesk-sdk` is an **unofficial** client for PatientDesk's Turkish voice
models. It wraps **Alania** text-to-speech and **Duyu** speech-to-text, the
account/catalog endpoints (`/v1/voices`, `/v1/pronunciations`, `/v1/styles`,
`/v1/alania/models`, usage) and keyless health checks. It has zero runtime
dependencies and uses the global `fetch`, `FormData`, `Blob` and `WebSocket`,
all of which can be injected.

> Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by PatientDesk. It is an
> independent client for their public, OpenAI-compatible API.

## Overview

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  install[Install package] --> client[new PatientDesk]
  client --> tts["speech.create()<br/>Alania TTS"]
  client --> stt["audio.transcribe()<br/>Duyu STT"]
  client --> stream["speech.stream() / socket()<br/>transcribeStream()"]
  client --> account["voices / pronunciations<br/>styles / models / usage"]
  client --> status["fetchStatus()<br/>fetchAlaniaHealth()"]
```

**Need:** [Node.js 20+](https://nodejs.org/), an API key from
[speech.patientdesk.ai](https://speech.patientdesk.ai). Deno, Bun and edge
runtimes work too, since only standard globals are used.

## 1. Install

```sh
npm install patientdesk-sdk
```

## 2. Set the API key

The client reads `PATIENDESK_API_KEY`, falling back to `PATIENDESK_KEY`. You can
also pass it directly to the constructor.

```sh
# macOS / Linux
export PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."

# Windows PowerShell
$env:PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."
```

## 3. First request

```ts
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

// Text to speech (Alania). The SDK defaults to alania-v1 (24 kHz) for backward
// compatibility; pass model: "alania-v2" for the API's current default (48 kHz).
const speech = await pd.speech.create({
  input: "Randevunuz oluşturuldu.",
  response_format: "wav",
});
const wav = new Uint8Array(await speech.arrayBuffer());

// Speech to text (Duyu)
const { text } = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: wav,
  audio_format: "wav",
  language: "tr",
});
console.log(text);
```

Alania can return `wav`, `mp3`, `opus`, `flac`, `aac`, `pcm`, `mulaw` or `alaw`
with `response_format`. For low-latency playback read [Streaming](streaming.md).
For microphone capture and live captions read [Node.js recipes](recipes.md).

## 4. Health check (no key)

```ts
import { fetchStatus, fetchAlaniaHealth, isOperational, statusDescription } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const status = await fetchStatus();
console.log(statusDescription(status)); // "All Systems Operational"
console.log(isOperational(status) ? "up" : "degraded");

const health = await fetchAlaniaHealth(); // GET /health/alania, per-model status
console.log(health.status, health.models?.["alania-v2"]?.status);
```

## What is on the client

| Member | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pd.speech` | `SpeechApi` | Alania text-to-speech, HTTP streaming and the WebSocket session. |
| `pd.audio` | `AudioApi` | Duyu speech-to-text, multipart REST and WebSocket streaming. |
| `pd.voices` | `VoicesApi` | List, save and delete voices (`/v1/voices`). |
| `pd.pronunciations` | `PronunciationsApi` | Manage the saved pronunciation dictionary. |
| `pd.styles` | `StylesApi` | List the ready-made style ids. |
| `pd.models` | `ModelsApi` | List the Alania model catalog. |
| `pd.usage()` | `Promise<UsageResponse>` | Account quota usage. |
| `pd.baseUrl` | `string` | Resolved API base URL. |
| `pd.origin` | `string` | HTTPS origin (no `/v1`), for health checks. |
| `pd.apiKey` | `string` | Resolved API key. |
| `pd.fetchImpl` | `typeof fetch` | The `fetch` in use. |
| `pd.wsImpl` | `WebSocketConstructor` | The `WebSocket` in use, if any. |

## Where to go next

- [Node.js recipes](recipes.md): speak, transcribe a file, use the microphone.
- [Text to speech](text-to-speech.md): every Alania parameter and output shape.
- [Speech to text](speech-to-text.md): formats, timestamps, subtitles.
- [Streaming](streaming.md): HTTP streaming and both WebSocket sessions.
- [Errors](errors.md): retries, backoff and rate limits.
- [Testing](testing.md): how to run the offline and live suites.

## Not sure it is us

Add `PATIENDESK_BASE_URL` to point the client at a proxy or a mock, and inject a
custom `fetch`. See [Configuration](configuration.md).

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/text-to-speech.md

# Text to speech

Alania is PatientDesk's text-to-speech model. One endpoint, `POST /audio/speech`,
takes JSON and returns the audio itself as the response body.

> **Default model:** PatientDesk's API now defaults to `alania-v2` (48 kHz). This
> SDK keeps sending `alania-v1` + `alania` (24 kHz) unless you pass a model, so
> existing code does not change. Pass `model: "alania-v2"` for the current model.

## Basic call

```ts
const speech = await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  voice: "alania2-f1",
  input: "Yarın saat 14:05 için randevunuz var.",
  response_format: "mp3",
});

speech.contentType;   // "audio/mpeg"
speech.disclosure;    // "ai-generated" (x-disclosure)
speech.model;         // "alania-v2" (x-model)
speech.characters;    // billed characters (x-characters; 0 for antalia-mini)
speech.audioSeconds;  // x-audio-seconds (absent while streaming)
speech.queueWaitMs;   // x-queue-wait-ms
```

`create()` returns a `SpeechResponse`, a thin view over the one response body.

| Member | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | `Response` | The raw response. Its body can be read once. |
| `contentType` | `string` | From the `Content-Type` header, or the format table. |
| `disclosure` | `string \| null` | `x-disclosure`, normally `ai-generated`. |
| `requestId` | `string \| null` | `x-request-id`; share it in support requests. |
| `model` | `string \| null` | `x-model`. |
| `characters` | `number \| null` | Billed characters. |
| `audioSeconds` | `number \| null` | Duration of the generated audio. |
| `queueWaitMs` | `number \| null` | Time spent waiting for a generation slot. |
| `sampleRate` | `number \| null` | Parsed from `Content-Type` (`rate=`), when present. |
| `arrayBuffer()` | `Promise<ArrayBuffer>` | Whole audio. |
| `blob()` | `Promise<Blob>` | Whole audio with the right `type`. |
| `stream()` | `ReadableStream<Uint8Array> \| null` | The raw body stream. |

Read the body **once**. Pick one of `arrayBuffer`, `blob` or `stream`.

## Common parameters

| Field | Type | SDK default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `string` | required | Up to 5,000 characters. Longer text throws `RangeError`. |
| `model` | `string` | `"alania-v1"` | `alania-v2`, `alania-v1`, `antalia-mini` (free). The API's own default is `alania-v2`. |
| `voice` | `string` | model's voice | Defaults: `alania` (v1), `alania2-f1` (v2), `antalia-mini`. One of the built-ins (see Built-in voices), a voice name, or a saved voice id. |
| `response_format` | `TtsFormat` | `"wav"` | `wav`, `mp3`, `opus`, `flac`, `aac`, `pcm`, `mulaw`, `alaw`. |
| `sample_rate` | `number` | model's rate | `8000`, `16000`, `22050`, `24000`, `44100`, `48000` (capped at the model). G.711 defaults to 8000. |
| `temperature` | `number` | server side | v1: 0–2.0 (default 0.30) · v2: 0.6–2.0 (default 1.0). |
| `seed` | `number` | unset | Same text + seed + settings reproduce the same audio. |
| `stream` | `boolean` | `false` | Stream the audio as it is generated; see [Streaming](streaming.md). |
| `extra` | `Record<string, unknown>` | unset | Merged into the body for forward compatibility. |

## Built-in voices

| Voice | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `alania2-f1` | Female, Alania-2's default voice. |
| `alania2-nisa` | Female, gentle and playful. |
| `alania2-oncel` | Male, mature and reassuring. The default male voice. |
| `alania2-m1` | Male. |
| `alania2-emre` | Male, smooth and thoughtful. |
| `alania2-fikri` | Male, clear and gentle. |
| `alania2-sezgin` | Male, soft-spoken and breathy. |
| `alania2-selin` | Female, relaxed and friendly. |
| `alania2-lina` | Female, warm and calm. |
| `alania2-melisa` | Female, bright and energetic. |
| `alania2-nil` | Female, warm and enthusiastic. |
| `alania` | Alania-1 male, only with `model: "alania-v1"` (the request alias for `alania-v1`). |
| `antalia-mini` | Antalia-2 Mini male, the free model. Use it with `model: "antalia-mini"`, or with this voice and no model. |

The named voices also accept their bare name (`"nisa"`, `"öncel"` or `"oncel"`
for Öncel, or `"male"` / `"erkek"`). `alania2-m2` and `alania2-f2` were retired
on 12 October 2026, so requests naming them get `400 unknown_voice`. The nine
named voices are designed voices (no actor recordings), each speaking from its
own fixed reference. They are not trained into the model, so with a style or an
`instructions` they drift a little further from their own timbre than
`alania2-f1` and `alania2-m1` do.

## Alania-2 fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | `string` | Ready style id: `support-warm`, `support-calm`, `sales-energetic`, `reception-smile` (`pd.styles.list()`). Cannot combine with `instructions`/`voice_description`. |
| `instructions` | `string` | How to speak, ≤200 characters, no parentheses. Non-English is translated. |
| `voice_description` | `string` | Design a new voice from a description, ≤200 characters. Combine with `seed` to reproduce it. |
| `reference_audio` | `Uint8Array \| ArrayBuffer \| Blob \| string` | Clone from a 3–30 s sample (≤10 MB); bytes or base64/data URI. |
| `reference_text` | `string` | Transcript of the sample (≤1,000 chars). Accepted, not used. |
| `consent` | `boolean` | Required with `reference_audio`: declares the speaker consented. |
| `pronunciations` | `object \| array` | Per-request overrides, e.g. `{ PatientDesk: "Peyşınt Desk" }` (≤200). Beats the saved dictionary. |
| `cfg` | `number` | 1.0–5.0 guidance strength (default 2.0, design 3.0). |
| `top_p` | `number` | alania-v1 only (0.01–1.0, default 0.9); alania-v2 ignores it. |

Sending an Alania-2 field with `model: "alania-v1"` is rejected with
`unsupported_field`, not silently ignored. Likewise `instructions` +
`voice_description` (or `style`) is rejected with `conflicting_fields`.

## Output formats

| `response_format` | `contentType` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wav` | `audio/wav` | 16-bit mono; 48 kHz (v2) or 24 kHz (v1). |
| `pcm` | `audio/L16` | Headerless; the rate is in `Content-Type` (`audio/L16; rate=48000`). |
| `mulaw` | `audio/PCMU` | Headerless G.711, one byte per sample, 8 kHz by default. |
| `alaw` | `audio/PCMA` | Same, A-law. |
| `mp3` | `audio/mpeg` | |
| `opus` | `audio/ogg` | |
| `flac` | `audio/flac` | |
| `aac` | `audio/aac` | |

When the server sends a `Content-Type`, it wins over the table.

## Streaming

```ts
// Yields PCM as it is generated. Strips the streamed WAV header and carries a
// sample split across network chunks.
for await (const pcm of pd.speech.stream({ model: "alania-v2", input: longText })) {
  player.write(pcm); // 48 kHz mono PCM16 (24 kHz for alania-v1)
}
```

`createRaw()` skips the wrapper: pass `stream: true` and read `response.body`
yourself. Only `wav`, `pcm`, `mulaw` and `alaw` stream. Compressed formats
return 400. For many sentences over one connection, use the WebSocket session,
see [Streaming](streaming.md).

## Splitting long text

Alania accepts at most 5,000 characters. Split on sentence boundaries and join
the resulting files with `ffmpeg` if you need a single recording.

```ts
const chunks = splitBySentence(longText, 5000);
for (const [i, chunk] of chunks.entries()) {
  const speech = await pd.speech.create({ input: chunk, response_format: "mp3" });
  await Deno.writeFile(`part-${i}.mp3`, new Uint8Array(await speech.arrayBuffer()));
}
```

## Saving voices

A clone or a design can be saved once and then used by id:

```ts
await pd.voices.save({ name: "Sesim", file: sampleBytes, consent: true });
await pd.voices.save({ name: "Danışman", voice_description, seed: 4242, input: designText });
await pd.speech.create({ model: "alania-v2", voice: savedId, input: "Merhaba" });
```

## Errors

Invalid local input throws before any request: `TypeError` for an empty `input`,
`RangeError` for text over 5,000 characters or a `reference_audio` over 10 MB.
Request failures throw `PatientDeskError`. See [Errors](errors.md).

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/speech-to-text.md

# Speech to text

Duyu is PatientDesk's speech-to-text model. The public endpoint is
`POST /audio/transcriptions` and it takes **multipart/form-data** with a `file`
field. Up to 100 MB / 2 hours per request. Longer audio is split server-side.
`audioBase64` is still accepted by the SDK: it is decoded locally and uploaded
as the same `file` part.

## Basic call

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const { text } = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: readFileSync("kayit.m4a"),
  audio_format: "m4a",   // names the upload; the server detects the format
  language: "tr",        // "tr" (default) or "auto"
  prompt: "ilaç: parol", // optional spelling hint
});
console.log(text);
```

You can pass raw bytes, an `ArrayBuffer` or a `Blob`. `audio_format` only names
the uploaded file (extension + MIME type). Duyu detects the real container from
the first bytes, so omitting it is safe.

## Parameters

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `audio` | `Uint8Array \| ArrayBuffer \| Blob` | none | Provide `audio` or `audioBase64`. |
| `audioBase64` | `string` | none | Pre-encoded audio; decoded locally, data URL prefix allowed. |
| `model` | `string` | `"duyu-1"` | `whisper-1` is accepted for compatibility. |
| `audio_format` | `SttFormat` | detected | `wav`, `mp3`, `m4a`, `webm`, `ogg`, `flac`; names the upload. |
| `language` | `string` | `"tr"` | `tr`, `auto`, or a full code. |
| `prompt` | `string` | unset | Names, drug names, ID formats. |
| `temperature` | `number` | `0` | Between 0 and 1. |
| `response_format` | `SttResponseFormat` | `"json"` | `json`, `text`, `verbose_json`, `srt`, `vtt`. |
| `timestamp_granularities` | `("segment" \| "word")[]` | unset | Only with `verbose_json`. |
| `extra` | `Record<string, unknown>` | unset | Merged into the form fields. |

The maximum audio size is 100 MB (and 2 hours) per request. The SDK rejects
larger input locally with a `RangeError`.

## Response shapes

`response_format` decides the return type, and the overloads reflect it.

| `response_format` | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| omitted or `json` | `Transcription` |
| `verbose_json` | `Transcription` with `segments` and `words` |
| `text`, `srt`, `vtt` | `string` |

```ts
// verbose_json -> segments and word timings
const detailed = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: bytes,
  response_format: "verbose_json",
  timestamp_granularities: ["word"],
});
for (const w of detailed.words ?? []) {
  console.log(`${w.start.toFixed(2)}s ${w.word}`);
}

// srt -> the subtitle text itself
const srt = await pd.audio.transcribe({ audio: bytes, response_format: "srt" });
```

The `Transcription` shape:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | The transcript. |
| `task` | `string` | e.g. `transcribe`. |
| `language` | `string` | Detected or requested language. |
| `duration` | `number` | Seconds; this is the billed duration. |
| `segments` | `TranscriptionSegment[]` | With `verbose_json`. |
| `words` | `TranscriptionWord[]` | With `verbose_json` and word granularity. |

## Base64 helper

`toBase64()` is exported if you need to build a payload yourself, and
`fromBase64()` decodes one. A `data:` URL prefix is stripped automatically.

```ts
import { toBase64 } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const b64 = toBase64(new Uint8Array(buf)); // no data: prefix
await pd.audio.transcribe({ audioBase64: b64, audio_format: "wav" });
```

## Live transcription

For microphone use, the WebSocket session is lower latency than the REST call:
draft `partial` transcripts while speaking, a `final` line after the sentence,
and `vad`/`segment_*` events. It is documented and lives on its own page:
[Streaming](streaming.md).

## Service-side decodes

PatientDesk's REST endpoint has been observed returning `400 undecodable_audio`,
or a bundled internal stack trace, for perfectly valid files. Those are upstream
faults. The live suite labels them for you, see [Testing](testing.md).

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/streaming.md

# Streaming

Three streaming paths are documented by PatientDesk. The SDK wraps all of them:

| Path | API | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP TTS | `pd.speech.stream()` | One long text, play as it is generated. |
| WebSocket TTS | `pd.speech.socket()` | Many sentences over one connection (voice assistants). |
| WebSocket STT | `pd.audio.transcribeStream()` | Live microphone / phone audio, draft + final transcripts. |

## HTTP streaming (TTS)

```ts
for await (const pcm of pd.speech.stream({
  model: "alania-v2",
  input: longText,
  response_format: "pcm", // wav | pcm | mulaw | alaw only
})) {
  player.write(pcm);      // 48 kHz mono PCM16 (24 kHz for alania-v1)
}
```

- A streamed `wav` response starts with a 44-byte RIFF header whose length fields
  are `0xFFFFFFFF`, and the helper strips it.
- Network chunks can split a sample: the helper carries the leftover byte into
  the next frame.
- Long text is split at sentence boundaries server-side, with 250 ms of silence
  between parts.
- `mp3`, `opus`, `flac` and `aac` cannot stream, those requests return 400.

`createRaw({ stream: true })` returns the raw `Response` if you want to handle
the body yourself.

## WebSocket (TTS)

`wss://voice.patientdesk.ai/v1/audio/speech/stream` keeps one connection open and
speaks sentences in order. Auth is `?key=` (or `{ token }` for a session token).

```ts
const socket = pd.speech.socket(
  {
    ready: (info) => console.log(info.model, info.sampleRate),
    speechStart: (info) => console.log(info.characters, "chars, disclosure", info.raw.disclosure),
    audio: (chunk) => player.write(chunk),   // binary PCM16 or G.711
    speechEnd: (info) => console.log(info.audioSeconds, "s,", info.inferMs, "ms"),
  },
  { model: "alania-v2", encoding: "mulaw", sampleRate: 8000 },
);

await socket.speak({ input: "Randevunuz oluşturuldu." }); // queued until `ready`
socket.stop();  // `speech_end` + `stopped` arrive, then the server closes
await socket.closed;
```

`speak()` accepts the same fields as `speech.create()` and messages are processed
one at a time. The connection can set `model`, `encoding` (`pcm_s16le`, `mulaw`,
`alaw`) and `sample_rate` for every message.

## WebSocket (STT)

`wss://voice.patientdesk.ai/v1/audio/stream` takes raw PCM and emits a `final`
transcript shortly after each sentence ends. Auth is `?key=` (or `{ token }`).

```ts
const stream = pd.audio.transcribeStream(
  {
    ready: (info) => console.log("quota", info.quota),
    vad: (info) => (meter.level = info.active ? 1 : 0),
    partial: (draft) => console.log("…", draft),
    final: (text, raw) => console.log(text, raw.start, raw.end, raw.audio_s, raw.rtf),
    stopped: (info) => console.log("billed", info.audioSeconds),
    error: (message) => console.error(message),
  },
  { sampleRate: 16000, eagerFinal: true, partials: true, partialMs: 200 },
);

stream.sendAudio(pcmChunk); // raw 16-bit PCM, mono
stream.stop();              // finalizes the open sentence, then the server closes
await stream.closed;
```

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sampleRate` | `16000` | Input rate; the server resamples (8 kHz telephony works). |
| `eagerFinal` | `true` | Finalize without waiting for the silence threshold (~120 ms sooner). |
| `partials` | off | Ask for draft `partial` events while a sentence is spoken. |
| `partialMs` | server | Draft interval in milliseconds. |
| `token` | unset | Use `?token=` instead of the API key. |
| `extra` | unset | Merged into the `start` frame. |

Events: `ready` (`model`, `quota.remaining_s`), `vad` (`prob`, `active`),
`segment_start`, `partial`, `segment_end`, `final` (`text`, `start`, `end`,
`audio_s`, `infer_ms`, `rtf`), `stopped` (`audio_s`), `error`, `close`.

With 40–100 ms of audio per binary frame the server has enough to work with.
`examples/stt-live.mjs` does exactly that.

## Requirements

Streaming needs a `WebSocket` implementation. In Node 20 and 21 there is no
global `WebSocket`, so inject one. From Node 22 the global exists.

```ts
import WebSocket from "ws";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, WebSocket });
```

If no implementation is available, `transcribeStream()` / `socket()` throws a
`PatientDeskError` with code `no_websocket` before opening anything.

## Known flakiness

The Websocket handshake is intermittently refused: a fresh socket sometimes
closes with code `1006` before the `ready` frame. Retry two or three times before
treating it as a client bug, the live suites do exactly that.

Authentication is passed in the URL for a browser `WebSocket`, which cannot set
headers. Treat the URL as a secret and do not log it.

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/recipes.md

# Node.js recipes

Real-life examples for the two things people build first: speak text, and turn
speech into text. Every recipe is a runnable file under [`examples/`](../examples)
and needs no npm dependency. The only external tool is `ffmpeg` (with `ffplay`)
for recording and playback.

```sh
# macOS / Linux
export PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."

# Windows PowerShell
$env:PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."
```

Install ffmpeg if you do not have it:

```sh
# Windows
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg

# macOS
brew install ffmpeg

# Debian or Ubuntu
sudo apt install ffmpeg
```

| Recipe | File | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speak and play | `examples/tts.mjs` | Alania to a file, then plays it. `--stream` plays while it downloads. |
| Transcribe a file | `examples/stt-file.mjs` | Duyu over REST, with `verbose_json`, `srt` and `vtt`. |
| Record then transcribe | `examples/stt-mic.mjs` | Records the microphone with ffmpeg, then transcribes it. |
| Live microphone | `examples/stt-live.mjs` | Streams the microphone to Duyu over WebSocket. |

## Speak text and hear it

The shortest path: one call, save the bytes, play the file.

```ts
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const run = promisify(execFile);
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

async function speak(text: string) {
  const speech = await pd.speech.create({ input: text, response_format: "wav" });
  await writeFile("randevu.wav", new Uint8Array(await speech.arrayBuffer()));
  // ffplay ships with ffmpeg and plays on every desktop OS.
  await run("ffplay", ["-autoexit", "-nodisp", "-loglevel", "quiet", "randevu.wav"]);
}

await speak("Randevunuz yarın saat 14:05 için oluşturuldu.");
```

This uses the SDK's default `alania-v1` (24 kHz). For the API's current model,
pass `model: "alania-v2"`, `voice: "alania2-f1"` and optionally a `style` or
`instructions`, see [Text to speech](text-to-speech.md).

### Low latency playback

For a voice assistant you want audio to start before the whole file arrives.
`pd.speech.stream()` yields PCM as it is generated, with the WAV header already
stripped and split samples carried over.

```ts
import { Readable } from "node:stream";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

async function speakStreaming(text: string) {
  const chunks = pd.speech.stream({ model: "alania-v2", input: text, response_format: "pcm" });

  const player = spawn("ffplay", [
    "-autoexit", "-nodisp", "-loglevel", "quiet",
    "-f", "s16le", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "1", "-i", "-",
  ]);
  Readable.from(chunks).pipe(player.stdin);
  await new Promise((resolve) => player.on("close", resolve));
}

await speakStreaming("Bir saniye, kaydınızı kontrol ediyorum.");
```

`pcm` is uncompressed 16-bit mono. The rate is 48 kHz for `alania-v2` and
`antalia-mini`, 24 kHz for `alania-v1`, and it is also in the `Content-Type`
header (`audio/L16` with `rate=48000`) when you use `createRaw()`.

Run it:

```sh
node examples/tts.mjs "Randevunuz oluşturuldu."
node examples/tts.mjs "Merhaba" --stream
```

## Transcribe a file

Send the bytes and read the transcript. The SDK uploads them as
`multipart/form-data` for you.

```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

const audio = await readFile("kayit.m4a");
const { text, language, duration } = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: new Uint8Array(audio),
  audio_format: "m4a",
  language: "tr",
});

console.log(`${language} ${duration}s`);
console.log(text);
```

For subtitles, ask for `srt` or `vtt` and write the string straight to a file.

```ts
const srt = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: new Uint8Array(await readFile("interview.mp3")),
  response_format: "srt",
});
await writeFile("interview.srt", srt);
```

Run it:

```sh
node examples/stt-file.mjs kayit.m4a
node examples/stt-file.mjs kayit.wav --verbose
node examples/stt-file.mjs interview.mp3 --format srt > interview.srt
```

## Record from the microphone, then transcribe

There is no bundled microphone API, but ffmpeg captures the default input on
every platform. Record a WAV, then send it.

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

function record(seconds: number, out: string) {
  // Windows needs a DirectShow device name. Use "ffmpeg -f dshow -list_devices true -i dummy"
  // to find it, or see examples/audio.mjs which discovers it for you.
  const input =
    process.platform === "darwin"
      ? ["-f", "avfoundation", "-i", ":0"]
      : process.platform === "win32"
        ? ["-f", "dshow", "-i", `audio=${process.env.MIC_DEVICE}`]
        : ["-f", "alsa", "-i", "default"];

  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const ff = spawn("ffmpeg", [
      "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y",
      ...input,
      "-t", String(seconds),
      "-ar", "16000", "-ac", "1",
      out,
    ]);
    ff.on("close", (code) => (code === 0 ? resolve(out) : reject(new Error(`ffmpeg ${code}`))));
  });
}

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

await record(5, "mic.wav");
const { text } = await pd.audio.transcribe({
  audio: new Uint8Array(await readFile("mic.wav")),
  audio_format: "wav",
  language: "tr",
});
console.log(text);
```

`examples/audio.mjs` wraps this, including device discovery on Windows.

Run it:

```sh
node examples/stt-mic.mjs 5
node examples/stt-mic.mjs 5 --keep --out kayit.wav
```

## Live microphone over WebSocket

For a live assistant, streaming is lower latency than record-then-send. Read
[Streaming](streaming.md) first for the full event set.

```ts
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY });

const stream = pd.audio.transcribeStream({
  partial: (draft) => process.stdout.write(`\r… ${draft}`),
  final: (text) => console.log("\nfinal:", text),
  error: (message) => console.error(message),
});

// 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit PCM, exactly what the endpoint expects.
const ff = spawn("ffmpeg", [
  "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error",
  "-f", "avfoundation", "-i", ":0",
  "-ar", "16000", "-ac", "1", "-f", "s16le", "-",
]);
ff.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => stream.sendAudio(new Uint8Array(chunk)));

process.on("SIGINT", () => {
  ff.kill("SIGKILL");
  stream.stop();
});
await stream.closed;
```

Run it:

```sh
node examples/stt-live.mjs 10
```

Node 22 and later ship a global `WebSocket`. On older versions pass one to the
client: `new PatientDesk({ apiKey, WebSocket })`.

## Telling "us" from PatientDesk

If a valid file comes back as `undecodable_audio`, it is a service-side decode
error and not your input. Check the service first, then retry.

```ts
import { fetchStatus, isOperational } from "patientdesk-sdk";

if (!isOperational(await fetchStatus())) {
  console.warn("PatientDesk is degraded, try again later");
}
```

See [Testing](testing.md) for how the live suite attributes these faults, and
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for the common messages.

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/configuration.md

# Configuration

All client options are optional except the API key, which can come from the
environment.

## Constructor

```ts
import { PatientDesk } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const pd = new PatientDesk({
  apiKey: process.env.PATIENDESK_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: "https://voice.patientdesk.ai/v1",
  maxRetries: 2,
  timeout: 120_000,
  defaultHeaders: { "x-app": "my-clinic" },
});
```

## Options

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiKey` | `string` | `PATIENDESK_API_KEY`, then `PATIENDESK_KEY` | Required. Missing throws. |
| `baseUrl` | `string` | `https://voice.patientdesk.ai/v1` | Trailing slashes are trimmed. |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | global `fetch` | Inject for tests or edge runtimes. |
| `WebSocket` | `WebSocketConstructor` | global `WebSocket` | Needed for streaming STT and the TTS socket. |
| `maxRetries` | `number` | `2` | Retries for 429, 5xx and network errors. `quota_exceeded` is never retried. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `120000` | Per-request milliseconds. `0` disables. |
| `defaultHeaders` | `Record<string, string>` | `{}` | Merged into every request. |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Read by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PATIENDESK_API_KEY` | `PatientDesk`, `full-test`, `fixtures` | Preferred key. |
| `PATIENDESK_KEY` | same | Fallback if the first is unset. |
| `PATIENDESK_BASE_URL` | live tests | Override the API base URL. |
| `PATIENDESK_ALLOW_API_FAULTS` | live tests | `1` downgrades PatientDesk faults to skipped. |

## Constants and exports

| Export | Value | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://voice.patientdesk.ai/v1` | |
| `DEFAULT_ORIGIN` | `https://voice.patientdesk.ai` | Used by `fetchAlaniaHealth`. |
| `DEFAULT_STATUS_URL` | `https://status.patientdesk.ai/api/v2/status.json` | |
| `RETRYABLE_STATUS` | a `ReadonlySet<number>` | `408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504`. |
| `MAX_INPUT_CHARS` | `5000` | Alania input limit. |
| `MAX_REFERENCE_BYTES` | `10 * 1024 * 1024` | Voice-clone sample limit. |
| `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` | `100 * 1024 * 1024` | Duyu audio limit per request. |
| `CONTENT_TYPE` | a format to MIME map | Used by `SpeechResponse.contentType`. |

## Custom `fetch`

Useful for logging, tests or a proxy. Any function with the `fetch` signature is
accepted.

```ts
const pd = new PatientDesk({
  apiKey,
  fetch: (input, init) => {
    console.log(input);
    return fetch(input, init);
  },
});
```

## Custom `WebSocket`

Node 20 and 21 have no global `WebSocket`. Inject one for `transcribeStream()`
and `speech.socket()`.

```ts
import WebSocket from "ws";

const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, WebSocket });
```

## Edge runtimes

Because the SDK uses globals and has no dependencies, it runs on Cloudflare
Workers, Deno and Bun. Provide `apiKey` explicitly on runtimes without
`process.env`.

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/errors.md

# Errors

Every non-2xx response, and every transport failure the client wraps, throws a
`PatientDeskError`. It carries the parsed PatientDesk error shape plus the
rate-limit fields, so you can schedule a retry from `resetsAt`.

## Catching

```ts
import { PatientDeskError } from "patientdesk-sdk";

try {
  await pd.speech.create({ input: "x" });
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof PatientDeskError) {
    console.error(err.status, err.code, err.message);
    if (err.isRateLimit) {
      console.log(`quota (${err.scope}) resets at ${err.resetsAt}`);
    }
  }
}
```

## Fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `number` | HTTP status. `0` for a transport or timeout failure. |
| `code` | `string \| undefined` | e.g. `rate_limit_error`, `model_retired`. |
| `body` | `unknown` | Parsed error body, when it was JSON. |
| `reason` | `string \| undefined` | `error.details.reason`. |
| `scope` | `string \| undefined` | `user` or `pool`. |
| `retryAfterSeconds` | `number \| undefined` | From `Retry-After` or `details`. |
| `resetAt` | `string \| undefined` | ISO time from `error.details.resetAt`. |
| `isRateLimit` | `boolean` (getter) | `true` when `status === 429`. |
| `resetsAt` | `Date \| null` (getter) | `resetAt`, or now plus `retryAfterSeconds`. |

`resetsAt` returns a `Date` when the server gave either a reset time or a retry
delay, and `null` otherwise.

## Local validation errors

These throw before any request and are not `PatientDeskError`:

| Error | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `TypeError` | Empty `input`, missing `audio`, empty audio, wrong audio type, empty `reference_audio`. |
| `RangeError` | `input` over 5,000 characters, `reference_audio` over 10 MB, audio over 100 MB. |

Client construction errors are `PatientDeskError`:

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `missing_api_key` | No key passed and no env var set. |
| `no_fetch` | No global `fetch` and none injected. |
| `no_websocket` | Streaming without a `WebSocket` implementation. |
| `no_base64` | No `btoa`/`Buffer` (encode) or `atob`/`Buffer` (decode) available. |

## Retries and backoff

The client retries automatically on `408`, `409`, `425`, `429`, `500`, `502`,
`503`, `504`, and on network failures. Everything else `4xx` is returned at once.

- Default `maxRetries` is `2`, so up to 3 attempts.
- `429 quota_exceeded` is **never** retried: waiting will not clear the monthly
  quota. Back off until the quota resets instead.
- When a `Retry-After` header is present, the wait is capped at 30 seconds.
- Otherwise the delay grows exponentially, base `250 ms`, capped at `4 s`, with a
  small jitter.

A timeout aborts the request after `timeout` milliseconds, `120000` by default.
Set `timeout: 0` to disable it.

```ts
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, maxRetries: 0, timeout: 30_000 });
```

## Mapping the message

The message comes from `error.message` in the body, then falls back to
`PatientDesk HTTP <status>`. The code comes from `error.code`.

## Reading the body once

The error is built from a clone of the response, so the original body is left
untouched. The client never retries a non-retryable `4xx`.

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/health-and-status.md

# Health and status

PatientDesk publishes a public Statuspage and an API health endpoint. The SDK
ships standalone helpers for both that take **no API key**, so a test run can
check service health before touching the paid endpoints.

## Statuspage

```
GET https://status.patientdesk.ai/api/v2/status.json
```

```ts
import { fetchStatus, isOperational, statusDescription } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const status = await fetchStatus();
console.log(statusDescription(status)); // "All Systems Operational"
if (!isOperational(status)) {
  throw new Error("PatientDesk is degraded, skipping live checks");
}
```

## API health

```
GET https://voice.patientdesk.ai/health/alania
```

Per-model status: a model is `degraded` while it is loading, and requests to it
answer `model_loading` until it is ready.

```ts
import { fetchAlaniaHealth } from "patientdesk-sdk";

const health = await fetchAlaniaHealth();
health.status;                          // "ok"
health.models?.["alania-v2"]?.status;   // "ok" | "degraded"
health.limits_degraded;                 // boolean
```

Pass `{ origin }` to point it at another host. Like `fetchStatus`, the helper
does not require a key.

## Functions

| Function | Returns | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchStatus(options?)` | `Promise<StatusResponse>` | Fetches and parses the Statuspage summary. |
| `fetchAlaniaHealth(options?)` | `Promise<AlaniaHealthResponse>` | Fetches `/health/alania`. |
| `isOperational(status)` | `boolean` | `false` when the indicator is not `none`. |
| `statusDescription(status)` | `string` | The human summary, or `"unknown"`. |

`isOperational` treats `minor`, `major`, `critical` and `maintenance` as
degraded. A missing indicator returns `false`.

## Options

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | the Statuspage endpoint | `fetchStatus` only: override the URL. |
| `origin` | `string` | `https://voice.patientdesk.ai` | `fetchAlaniaHealth` only: API origin. |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | global `fetch` | Inject a fetch. |
| `timeout` | `number` | `10000` | Milliseconds. `0` disables. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | unset | Cancel the request. |
| `retries` | `number` | `1` | Retries on network errors and 5xx. |

Unlike `PatientDesk.request`, these helpers do not wrap failures in
`PatientDeskError`. They throw the underlying error, which makes them easy to
call from a preflight script.

## Response shapes

Statuspage:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status.indicator` | `string` | `none`, `minor`, `major`, `critical`, `maintenance`. |
| `status.description` | `string` | e.g. `All Systems Operational`. |
| `page.name` | `string` | The status page name. |
| `page.updated_at` | `string` | ISO time of the last update. |

`/health/alania`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `string` | `ok` when the service is up. |
| `models` | `Record<string, { status, sample_rate, default }>` | Per-model status. |
| `limits_degraded` | `boolean` | Whether rate limits are relaxed/degraded. |

The full bodies are preserved, so any extra field is available.

## Using it as a preflight

`scripts/preflight.mjs` calls `fetchStatus`: it requires `PATIENDESK_API_KEY`,
checks the service, and stops the live suite with one message when the service is
not fully operational. See [Testing](testing.md).

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/0.2.0.md

# Upgrading to 0.2.0

This guide covers `patientdesk-sdk` `0.1.0` to `0.2.0`. The release is mostly
additive: the SDK keeps its Alania-1 defaults, so existing code keeps working.
The changes that can affect you are listed first, then the new features and the
migration recipes.

## At a glance

- Drop-in for most code. The SDK still sends `model: "alania-v1"` and
  `voice: "alania"` (24 kHz) unless you pass a model.
- Speech to text now uploads multipart instead of base64 JSON (`audioBase64` is
  still accepted and decoded locally).
- `transcribeStream().stop()` waits for the server to finalize the open sentence
  before closing, instead of closing immediately.
- Streaming auth now uses `?key=` (`{ token }` remains available for session
  tokens).
- `429 quota_exceeded` is not retried anymore.
- The audio limit is 100 MB (it was about 9 MB).
- Alania-2, streaming helpers and the account endpoints are new.

## Behaviour changes

### Speech to text uploads multipart

`0.1.0` sent the audio as base64 inside a JSON body. `0.2.0` follows the current
public contract: `multipart/form-data` with a `file` part.

```ts
// Unchanged for callers. Both forms work:
await pd.audio.transcribe({ audio: bytes, audio_format: "wav" });
await pd.audio.transcribe({ audioBase64: base64, audio_format: "wav" });
```

No caller code change is needed. If you wrap `fetch` with a proxy, middleware or
logger, be aware that the request body is now a `FormData` instance and the SDK
no longer sets a `content-type` header for it (the runtime sets the boundary).
`audioBase64` is decoded locally and uploaded as the same `file` part.

The limit is now 100 MB and 2 hours per request (`MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` exports the
new value). Longer audio is split server-side.

### stop() waits for the final transcript

`0.1.0` sent `{type:"stop"}` and closed the socket immediately, which could drop
the final transcript of the open sentence. `0.2.0` sends the stop frame, waits
for `final` plus `stopped`, and lets the server close. If the server never
answers, the SDK force-closes after 5 seconds so callers cannot hang.

```ts
stream.stop();
await stream.closed; // may take up to about 5 s when the server goes quiet
```

If you put your own timeout around `stream.closed`, keep it above 5 seconds.

### WebSocket authentication uses key

Both WebSocket sessions now authenticate with `?key=<apiKey>`, matching the
current documentation. The previous `?token=` parameter still exists as an
option for short-lived session tokens.

```ts
// API key (default)
pd.audio.transcribeStream(events);

// Session token
pd.audio.transcribeStream(events, { token: "session.jwt" });
```

The URL carries a secret either way. Do not log it.

### quota_exceeded is not retried

`0.1.0` retried every `429` with backoff. `0.2.0` returns `429 quota_exceeded`
immediately, because waiting does not clear a monthly quota. Other `429`
responses are still retried and honour `Retry-After`.

```ts
try {
  await pd.speech.create({ input: "x" });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.code === "quota_exceeded") {
    // Back off until err.resetsAt instead of retrying in a loop.
  }
}
```

### Temperature ranges are per model

| Model | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alania-v1` | 0 to 2.0 | 0.30 |
| `alania-v2` | 0.6 to 2.0 | 1.0 |

`top_p` is an Alania-1 field. `alania-v2` ignores it. Sending an Alania-2 field
with `model: "alania-v1"` is rejected with `unsupported_field` instead of being
silently ignored, and `instructions` cannot be combined with `voice_description`
or `style` (`conflicting_fields`).

## Migrating to Alania-2

Alania-2 is opt-in. Pass the model and a voice:

```ts
// 0.1.0 style, still valid
await pd.speech.create({ input: "Merhaba" });

// Alania-2, 48 kHz with the new voice set
const speech = await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  voice: "alania2-f1", // f1, m1, m2, f2
  input: "Merhaba",
});
```

If you pass `model: "alania-v2"` without `voice`, the SDK picks `alania2-f1`
automatically. The free model `antalia-mini` picks `antalia-mini` and bills zero
characters (`speech.characters` is 0).

### Style instructions and designed voices

```ts
await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  voice: "alania2-m1",
  style: "support-warm", // support-warm | support-calm | sales-energetic | reception-smile
  // or instructions: "speaking slowly and calmly"
  input: "Size nasıl yardımcı olabilirim?",
});

// Design a new voice from a description, keep the seed to reproduce it
await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  voice_description: "A warm, middle-aged woman with a low voice",
  seed: 4242,
  input: "Merhaba, randevunuzu yarın saat on dörde aldım.",
});
```

### Cloning voices

Inline clone on every request, or save once and reuse the id:

```ts
const speech = await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  input: "Bu ses, konuşanın izniyle kaydedildi.",
  reference_audio: sampleBytes, // 3 to 30 s, at most 10 MB
  consent: true,
});

const { id } = await pd.voices.save({ name: "Sesim", file: sampleBytes, consent: true });
await pd.speech.create({ model: "alania-v2", voice: id, input: "Merhaba" });
```

### Pronunciation dictionary

```ts
// Per request
await pd.speech.create({
  input: "PatientDesk ile görüşün.",
  pronunciations: { PatientDesk: "Peyşınt Desk" },
});

// Account-wide, applied to every request
await pd.pronunciations.add({ term: "PatientDesk", say_as: "Peyşınt Desk" });
```

### Telephony output

`mulaw` and `alaw` are new. They are headerless G.711 at 8 kHz by default.

```ts
const speech = await pd.speech.create({
  model: "alania-v2",
  input: "Görüşmeniz kayıt altına alınmaktadır.",
  response_format: "mulaw",
  sample_rate: 8000,
});
```

The full format set is now `wav`, `mp3`, `opus`, `flac`, `aac`, `pcm`, `mulaw`
and `alaw`. See [Text to speech](text-to-speech.md#output-formats).

## Migrating to streaming

### HTTP streaming

`0.1.0` required reading `response.body` yourself and handling the streamed WAV
header by hand. `speech.stream()` does both, including the byte carry when a
network chunk splits a sample.

```ts
for await (const pcm of pd.speech.stream({
  model: "alania-v2",
  input: longText,
  response_format: "pcm",
})) {
  player.write(pcm); // 48 kHz mono PCM16
}
```

Only `wav`, `pcm`, `mulaw` and `alaw` stream. Compressed formats return 400.

### WebSocket TTS

Speak many sentences over one connection instead of one request per sentence:

```ts
const socket = pd.speech.socket(
  {
    speechStart: (info) => console.log(info.characters),
    audio: (chunk) => player.write(chunk),
    speechEnd: (info) => console.log(info.audioSeconds),
  },
  { model: "alania-v2", encoding: "mulaw", sampleRate: 8000 },
);
await socket.speak({ input: "Randevunuz oluşturuldu." });
socket.stop();
await socket.closed;
```

### Live speech to text

The WebSocket stream is now documented and exposes the full event set:

```ts
const stream = pd.audio.transcribeStream(
  {
    partial: (draft) => showDraft(draft),
    final: (text, raw) => showFinal(text, raw.start, raw.end, raw.audio_s),
    stopped: (info) => console.log("billed", info.audioSeconds),
  },
  { sampleRate: 16000, eagerFinal: true, partials: true },
);
```

See [Streaming](streaming.md) for the options and the whole event list.

## New features in 0.2.0

| Feature | API |
| --- | --- |
| Alania-2 and the free `antalia-mini` | `model`, per-model default voice |
| Built-in voices and saved voices | `voice`, `pd.voices.list()` |
| Style, instructions, voice design | `style`, `instructions`, `voice_description` |
| Cloning | `reference_audio`, `consent`, `pd.voices.save()` |
| Pronunciation dictionary | `pronunciations`, `pd.pronunciations` |
| Guidance and sampling | `cfg`, `top_p`, `sample_rate`, `seed` |
| Telephony formats | `mulaw`, `alaw` |
| Billing and trace headers | `requestId`, `model`, `characters`, `audioSeconds`, `queueWaitMs` |
| HTTP streaming | `pd.speech.stream()` |
| WebSocket TTS | `pd.speech.socket()` |
| Live STT events | `partial`, `vad`, `segmentStart`, `segmentEnd`, `stopped` |
| Model catalog and styles | `pd.models.list()`, `pd.styles.list()` |
| Account usage | `pd.usage()` |
| API health | `fetchAlaniaHealth()` |

## Verifying the upgrade

```sh
npm test           # offline: unit and contract tests
npm run full-test  # live: needs PATIENDESK_API_KEY and an operational service
```

The live suite now also covers Alania-2 at 48 kHz, a ready style, the free
`antalia-mini` billing zero characters, the TTS WebSocket, and the read-only
catalog endpoints. If a request fails, check whether the message starts with
`SDK FAULT` or `PATIENDESK API FAULT`. See [Testing](testing.md).

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/0.2.1.md

# Upgrading to 0.2.1

This guide covers `patientdesk-sdk` `0.2.0` to `0.2.1`. The release has no
breaking API or type change. It tracks a change in PatientDesk's voice catalog.

## At a glance

- Alania-2 now ships 11 built-in voices. The nine named voices also accept
  their bare name (`"nisa"`, `"öncel"` or `"oncel"`).
- `alania2-m2` and `alania2-f2` were retired on 12 October 2026. Requests
  naming them now get `400 unknown_voice`.
- The `AlaniaVoice` type lists the current built-ins. Any string is still
  accepted, so existing code keeps compiling.
- The SDK defaults are unchanged: `alania-v1` + `alania`, or `alania2-f1` when
  you pass `model: "alania-v2"` without a voice.

## The new voice set

| Voice | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `alania2-f1` | Female, Alania-2's default voice. |
| `alania2-nisa` | Female, gentle and playful. |
| `alania2-oncel` | Male, mature and reassuring. The default male voice. |
| `alania2-m1` | Male. |
| `alania2-emre` | Male, smooth and thoughtful. |
| `alania2-fikri` | Male, clear and gentle. |
| `alania2-sezgin` | Male, soft-spoken and breathy. |
| `alania2-selin` | Female, relaxed and friendly. |
| `alania2-lina` | Female, warm and calm. |
| `alania2-melisa` | Female, bright and energetic. |
| `alania2-nil` | Female, warm and enthusiastic. |

The named voices are designed voices (no actor recordings), each speaking from
its own fixed reference. They are not trained into the model, so with a style
or an `instructions` they drift a little further from their own timbre than
`alania2-f1` and `alania2-m1` do. See
[Text to speech](text-to-speech.md) for the full set including `alania` and
`antalia-mini`.

## What to change

Replace a retired voice with `alania2-f1`, `alania2-oncel` or another built-in:

```ts
// Before (now 400 unknown_voice)
await pd.speech.create({ model: "alania-v2", voice: "alania2-m2", input: "Merhaba" });

// After
await pd.speech.create({ model: "alania-v2", voice: "alania2-oncel", input: "Merhaba" });
```

A voice name works in the same field:

```ts
await pd.speech.create({ model: "alania-v2", voice: "nisa", input: "Merhaba" });
```

## Backward compatibility

- `voice` accepts any string, so code that names a retired voice still compiles
  and sends the request as-is. The API answers `400 unknown_voice` right away.
  The SDK does not retry `4xx` responses.
- The SDK does not validate voice ids locally, so saved voices, clones and
  designs are unaffected.
- The default paths (`alania` for `alania-v1`, `alania2-f1` for `alania-v2`)
  are untouched.

## Verifying the upgrade

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

---

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/testing.md

# Testing

Testing is the point of this repository, so it is split in two suites on
purpose. One proves the SDK is correct with no key and no network. The other
proves it against the real service and names the faulty side when it breaks.

| Command | Needs key | Hits the network | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm test` | no | no | Unit and contract tests with a mock `fetch` and `WebSocket`. |
| `npm run full-test` | **yes** | **yes** | The unit suite, a preflight, then live tests. |

## Unit suite, `npm test`

Builds the package, then runs every file under `test/unit`. It injects a mock
`fetch` and a local WebSocket double, so it is deterministic and offline. It
covers:

- the client: auth headers, retries, backoff, timeouts, abort signals and
  `quota_exceeded` (never retried)
- TTS: body building, Alania-2 fields, per-model default voices, WAV-header
  stripping while streaming, the WebSocket socket, input validation
- STT: multipart uploads, every `response_format`, granularity fields, the
  100 MB limit
- streaming: `start` frames, every event (`partial`, `vad`, `segment_*`,
  `final`, `stopped`), graceful `stop()`
- account/catalog: voices, pronunciations, styles, models, usage, `/health/alania`
- errors: parsing, rate-limit fields, `resetsAt`
- status: indicators and descriptions
- down behavior: what happens when the service answers with an outage
- docwatch: sitemap filtering, article extraction, path mapping and unified diffs

Line coverage of the built ESM bundle is 100% (`node --test
--experimental-test-coverage` in `test/unit`). The CJS build is smoke-tested end
to end. The live suite closes the gap against the real service.

## Preflight

`npm run full-test` runs `scripts/preflight.mjs` before any live call. It:

1. requires `PATIENDESK_API_KEY`, otherwise exits non-zero with the exact
   PowerShell or shell line to set it
2. calls `fetchStatus` and checks `isOperational`
3. writes `test/.live-enabled=1` only on success

If either check fails it writes `0`, prints one actionable message, and stops.
Live tests do not run. There is never a silent green.

```sh
# macOS / Linux
export PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."
npm run full-test

# Windows PowerShell
$env:PATIENDESK_API_KEY="pd_live_..."
npm run full-test
```

## Deciding is it us or is it PatientDesk

Live failures are classified by fault party:

- `SDK FAULT while ...`: the request was well formed, so the failure is ours.
- `PATIENDESK API FAULT while ...`: PatientDesk surfaced its own internal error,
  for example `undecodable_audio` for a valid file, or a bundled stack trace.

Both **fail the run by default**, but the message names the culprit. The
classifier lives in `helpers/live.mjs` and matches known upstream patterns such
as `unexpected keyword`, `not subscriptable` and `Line N`.

To keep a genuine outage from looking like a broken repository, downgrade API
faults to skipped. They are still printed, never hidden:

```sh
PATIENDESK_ALLOW_API_FAULTS=1 npm run full-test
```

## Fixtures

Test fixtures under `test/fixtures/` are real Turkish speech generated with
Alania, converted with `ffmpeg` into `wav`, `m4a`, `mp3`, `ogg`, `webm`, `flac`
and 16 kHz raw PCM, plus a truncated clip that still decodes (the
upload-corruption path).

```sh
npm run fixtures
```

The script uses `PATIENDESK_API_KEY` when it is set. Without a key it writes a
synthetic tone so the offline layout is still complete, and it says so.

## Live suites

The live tests under `test/live/` cover TTS (including `alania-v2`, styles and
the free `antalia-mini`), the TTS WebSocket, STT over multipart REST, the STT
WebSocket stream, and the read-only catalog endpoints (`/v1/voices`,
`/v1/styles`, `/v1/alania/models`, usage, `/health/alania`). They read the
`.live-enabled` flag, so running them directly without preflight skips rather
than fails.

## Adding a test

Put offline tests in `test/unit` and import the built package from `dist`. Put
live tests in `test/live` and wrap the body with `guard(t, context, fn)` from
`helpers/live.mjs` so a service fault is attributed, not blamed on the SDK.

Source: https://groophylifefor.github.io/patientdesk-sdk/docs/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Every message below comes from a real path in the SDK or the test scripts. Start
here when something fails and the reason is not obvious.

## `Missing API key`

The client throws a `PatientDeskError` with code `missing_api_key` when neither
`apiKey` nor `PATIENDESK_API_KEY` nor `PATIENDESK_KEY` is set. Set the env var or
pass the key.

```ts
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey: "pd_live_..." });
```

## `No global fetch found`

The runtime has no `fetch`. Pass one, or upgrade to Node 20+.

```ts
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, fetch: myFetch });
```

## `No WebSocket available`

Streaming needs a `WebSocket`. Node 20 and 21 do not ship one. Inject `ws`.

```ts
import WebSocket from "ws";
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, WebSocket });
```

## `input is N characters`

Alania accepts at most 5,000 characters. Split the text and join the audio, see
[Text to speech](text-to-speech.md#splitting-long-text).

## STT returns `undecodable_audio`

This is a server-side error. The request was well formed, PatientDesk could not
decode the audio. It has been seen for valid WAV, MP3 and M4A files, and it was
confirmed with a working key on a fully operational service, so it is not a sign
of a bad file, a bad key or a bad SDK. The live suite labels it
`PATIENDESK API FAULT`.

Two message shapes appear. One is `[Errno 1094995529] Invalid data found when
processing input: '<none>'`, the other is a Python error such as
`open() got an unexpected keyword argument 'metadata_errors'`. Both mean the
same thing: the decode step failed inside the service.

Check the service first with `fetchStatus`. If it is operational and the error
persists, it is on PatientDesk's side. The `full-test` run reports it as
`PATIENDESK API FAULT while transcribing ...` and can be downgraded to skipped
with `PATIENDESK_ALLOW_API_FAULTS=1` while the outage lasts.

## STT returns an empty or unrelated transcript

A near-empty or silent file (for example a 44-byte WAV header with no audio) is
not rejected: the service has been observed answering `200` with `duration: 0`
and hallucinated text. Check `duration` (and your own silence detection) before
trusting a transcript. Genuinely undecodable bytes do return
`400 undecodable_audio`, which is the correct client error.

## Streaming never becomes ready

Both WebSocket sessions authenticate with a query parameter: `?key=` by default
(or `?token=` for a short-lived session token). The SDK sends `key`, pass
`{ token }` to use a token instead. If a socket connects and then just sits
there, check this first.

The handshake is also intermittently refused: a fresh socket sometimes closes
with code `1006` before `ready`, roughly one attempt in five. Retry two or three
times before treating it as a client bug.

When the connection is ready and you still get no `final`, check the audio. It
must be 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian PCM and contain speech. Silence,
tones or the wrong framing never produce a transcript.

`stop()` sends `{type:"stop"}` and **waits**: the server finalizes the open
sentence (`final` + `stopped`) and then closes. The SDK force-closes after 5
seconds if that never arrives, so callers cannot hang.

## `429` rate limit

The client raises a `PatientDeskError` with `isRateLimit` true. Read `scope` to
see whether it is a `user` or `pool` limit, and `resetsAt` for the reset time.
The client already retried twice, honouring `Retry-After`. Back off until
`resetsAt`, then retry.

`429 quota_exceeded` is not retried, the monthly quota does not clear by
waiting. The free `antalia-mini` model has its own limits (`429
free_limit_exceeded`) and does not consume quota.

```ts
if (err instanceof PatientDeskError && err.isRateLimit) {
  await sleep(err.resetsAt!.getTime() - Date.now());
}
```

## Requests hang

A request times out after `timeout` milliseconds, `120000` by default. Lower it
when a long call is not expected:

```ts
const pd = new PatientDesk({ apiKey, timeout: 30_000 });
```

An already-aborted `AbortSignal` fails immediately instead of hanging, so
cancellation is safe at any point.

## `full-test` does not run

The preflight stopped it. Either the key is missing, or the Statuspage is not
fully operational. The message names which. Unit tests still run with
`npm test`. If the service is degraded, retry later, or set
`PATIENDESK_ALLOW_API_FAULTS=1` to downgrade API faults to skipped.

## Live tests fail with `SDK FAULT`

That is a genuine bug in this repository. Read the context after `while`, which
names the operation, and open an issue with the full output. Do not set
`PATIENDESK_ALLOW_API_FAULTS` to hide it: that flag only affects API faults.

## Docs do not build

`npm run docs:build` needs the `marked` dev dependency. Run `npm install` first.
The generated HTML, `search-index.json`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and
`sitemap.xml` are written under `docs/`.
